criteria.no: There is no delivered compliance claim, or the claim has no checkable supporting artifact.
criteria.unclear: A cited artifact has an indeterminate connection to the compliance claim.
criteria.yes: A named test, command result, diff or path supports a claim that the exemption was delivered.

evidenced.instructions: Does `item.text` cite a concrete checkable artifact supporting delivered compliance with the same-name complementary-cfg sibling exemption across the required scopes?

criteria.no: The behavior is absent, expressly restricted to fewer scopes, or only promised for future delivery.
criteria.unclear: The behavior is mentioned but its adoption is explicitly unresolved or indeterminate.
criteria.yes: The text states the complete same-name complementary-cfg same-scope exemption across the three named scope forms.

implemented.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly state delivery of the required behavior: PORT-010 emits no finding for a cfg(unix) item paired with a same-name cfg(not(unix)) sibling in that same scope, for modules, inherent impls and crate roots? Judge the specific behavioral commitment only.

criteria.no: The task is outside PORT-010 and its fixtures; saying those are untouched is not involvement.
criteria.unclear: The described work cannot be located in a rule or fixture area.
criteria.yes: The work changes PORT-010 internals, sibling detection or port010 fixtures.

relevant.instructions: Does `item.text` work on PORT-010 implementation or its sibling regression fixtures? Include parser-internal refactoring of this rule even when sibling behavior is left unmentioned. Judge subject overlap only.

criteria.no: No opposing behavior is stated; silence, topical discussion or a future-only promise alone is not conflict.
criteria.unclear: The described behavior could either permit or forbid the required exemption.
criteria.yes: It explicitly retains findings for a qualifying pair in any required scope, including an invented scope exception.

violated.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly oppose the required behavior that PORT-010 emits no finding for a cfg(unix) item paired with a same-name cfg(not(unix)) sibling in that same scope, for modules, inherent impls and crate roots? Silence, unresolved discussion and deferred work alone do not establish conflict.

criteria.no: The report supplies only an assertion, a future promise, an incompatible outcome, or no supporting artifact.
criteria.unclear: Possible evidence is present but its support for delivered compliance is unclear.
criteria.yes: The delivery claim is backed by a test name/result, command/output, source path or diff.

evidenced.instructions: For a claim of delivered ANC-026 sibling handling in `item.text`, is there a named, checkable supporting artifact?

criteria.no: The obligation is omitted or expressly limited or rejected; future intentions do not describe accomplished work.
criteria.unclear: The topic appears but it is explicitly undecided whether the exemption is adopted.
criteria.yes: All required sibling conditions and module, inherent-impl and root coverage are present.

implemented.instructions: Is the following obligation substantively present as an accomplished change in `item.text`: PORT-010 emits no finding for a cfg(unix) item paired with a same-name cfg(not(unix)) sibling in that same scope, for modules, inherent impls and crate roots?

criteria.no: Only unrelated code or content is a work target.
criteria.yes: PORT-010 code or tests are a work target, including its parser allocations.

relevant.instructions: Is the work described by `item.text` within PORT-010 or its fixtures? Rule parser maintenance is relevant implementation work even if it does not state the required sibling behavior.

criteria.no: No such incompatible behavior is stated. Silence, deferral, unresolved decisions and tests of nonqualifying different-scope or different-cfg items do not establish incompatibility.
criteria.unclear: It cannot be determined whether stated behavior reports a qualifying pair.
criteria.yes: At least one of those qualifying scope forms intentionally still reports the item.

violated.instructions: Find an explicit incompatible PORT-010 behavior in `item.text`: would a same-name cfg(not(unix)) sibling in the same module, inherent impl or crate root still leave its cfg(unix) counterpart reported? Judge only stated incompatibility.

criteria.no: No delivered compliance claim is backed by an artifact; assertions and future commitments alone do not qualify.

criteria.yes: The report connects delivered sibling exemption to a concrete named test, executed command/output, source path or diff.

criteria.no: It does not supply that behavior, supplies only a subset, or describes future work alone.

criteria.yes: It expressly covers the complete required behavior, whether phrased as zero findings, exemption or suppression.

implemented.instructions: Does `item.text` say it achieved the anchor's exact sibling behavior: PORT-010 emits no finding for a cfg(unix) item paired with a same-name cfg(not(unix)) sibling in that same scope, for modules, inherent impls and crate roots?

criteria.no: It concerns another activity and leaves PORT-010 untouched.
criteria.unclear: The described activity does not identify an ascertainable area.
criteria.yes: It works on this rule or its fixtures, including rule-local parsing or boundary cases.

relevant.instructions: Does the account in `item.text` touch the PORT-010 implementation or regression tests that contain the same-name sibling behavior? Include internal refactoring that is silent about that behavior.

criteria.no: No qualifying pair is stated to remain reported. The report may instead exempt such pairs, omit the behavior, defer work or leave a decision unresolved.
